around.headline: Fake, expired medicines worth Rs 5 crore seized at a Bengaluru repacking unit; chemists say the racket bypasses retail chemists entirely
around.summary: Enforcement seized counterfeit and expired medicines worth about Rs 5 crore from a repacking unit, and Bengaluru chemists say such fake stock is unlikely to pass through licensed retail counters — pointing instead to hospitals and online sellers. Buy medicines only from a licensed pharmacy that gives a printed bill, and be wary of unusually cheap prices from online sellers.
around.source: The Times of India, NDTV, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Bengaluru woman loses Rs 4 lakh gold chain to thieves who used a festival crowd as cover
around.summary: Thieves stole a woman's Rs 4 lakh gold chain by exploiting the crush of a festival-day crowd, according to today's report. With Varamahalakshmi and other festival gatherings this week, avoid wearing visible gold jewellery in dense crowds, or keep it tucked under clothing.

around.headline: BMRCL's elevated Pink Line to open in September-end, safety inspection now underway
around.summary: The Pink Line is set to open by the end of September, with BMRCL preparing for the mandatory safety inspection before that. It's a genuine addition to Metro coverage — worth checking the route once it opens if it cuts your usual commute.

around.headline: Bengaluru's footpath encroachments to be cleared by August-end, minister says
around.summary: A state minister has said footpath encroachments across the city will be cleared by the end of this month, alongside a separate civic push on the city's 1,616 garbage blackspots. Residents say clearing alone hasn't made footpaths walkable elsewhere, so treat this as a promise to watch rather than a done deal.

around.headline: New government rules capping how many SIM cards you can hold take effect August 24
around.summary: New telecom rules limiting the number of SIM cards an individual can hold kick in from August 24. If you're carrying multiple numbers on one ID (work, personal, family), check which ones are registered in your name before the rule takes effect.

around.headline: Retail F&O traders paid Rs 25,000 crore in transaction costs in FY26 despite mostly losing money
around.summary: A new analysis shows retail futures-and-options traders paid roughly Rs 25,000 crore in transaction costs this financial year, even as most of them lost money overall. If you're trading options casually, the costs alone are a headwind before you even account for losses — a plain index SIP carries none of this drag.

around.headline: Karnataka CM tells Tamil Nadu and Puducherry that Mekedatu dam water — beyond 5 TMC for Bengaluru's drinking needs — will go to Tamil Nadu
around.summary: At a meeting convened by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar said he has committed that only 5 TMC of Mekedatu dam water will be kept back for drinking, with the rest released to Tamil Nadu. The dam is meant to secure Bengaluru's drinking water supply, so how this commitment plays out matters directly for the city's future water security.

street_smart.title: You're squeezed into a dense festival-day crowd near a temple or pandal, wearing your gold chain, when someone brushes hard against your neck from behind. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a Bengaluru woman had her Rs 4 lakh gold chain stolen by thieves who used a festival crowd as cover (The Times of India). Crowd/festival-rush theft hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — bike-borne chain snatching (Aug 13) was a different, open-road mechanism.
street_smart.situation: It's a festival day and the streets and temple approach are packed shoulder-to-shoulder. You're wearing a gold chain out of habit, and in the crush you can't tell who's standing behind you or whether the contact was accidental.

choices.text: Before stepping out on a festival day, tuck the chain under your collar or leave it at home; in the crowd itself, keep bags in front of you and stay alert to being boxed in by two or three people at once. If you feel a tug or sudden contact at your neck, shout immediately, push toward open ground or a shop/police point, and check right away — don't wait to 'see if it's really gone.'
choices.feedback: Correct, and the order matters. Removing the visible target beforehand denies the thief the opening entirely; shouting and moving the instant you feel contact interrupts the theft before the crowd swallows the moment. If it's already gone, report it the same day with a description — many streets and temple approaches run CCTV that's only kept for a limited number of days.

choices.text: Wear the chain as usual since it's an auspicious day and nothing has happened to you before.
choices.feedback: This is exactly the mechanism the theft depends on. Festival crowds are the preferred setting precisely because the crush of bodies disguises deliberate contact as accidental jostling, makes it nearly impossible to identify who touched you, and gives the thief a packed crowd to vanish into within seconds. Nothing happening before isn't safety — it's the setup that makes today's crowd look no different from any other.

choices.text: The moment you realise it's gone, push through the crowd yourself to chase down whoever was standing closest to you.
choices.feedback: You don't know if the person who brushed you was the thief, an accomplice creating the crowd, or someone unrelated — grabbing a stranger in a packed crowd risks a real physical fight or hitting the wrong person entirely, and it lets any actual thief close by simply keep moving with the crowd. Prioritise getting to open space and reporting with whatever description you have; let police work the CCTV.

choices.text: Post the incident and a request for tips on a local WhatsApp or social media group before filing a police complaint.
choices.feedback: The instinct to warn others is reasonable, but doing it before filing means there's no complaint number to anchor the post to, and crowdsourced 'tips' can misidentify an innocent bystander with no way to verify them. File first — a same-day report with time and location is also what gets CCTV footage pulled before it's overwritten.

choices.text: Say nothing at the time, and only mention it later if someone asks why you're not wearing the chain anymore.
choices.feedback: Delay costs you the two things that actually help: a fresh description while it's still clear in your memory, and CCTV footage from the spot, which many systems overwrite within days to weeks. A same-day report, even a brief one, keeps both available.

takeaways: Don't wear visible gold jewellery into a dense festival crowd — tuck it away or leave it home; the crush is the thief's cover, not yours.
If you feel sudden contact at your neck or bag, shout and move toward open space immediately — the theft depends on the crowd absorbing the moment before you react.
Report the same day with a time, location and description; a Zero FIR can be filed at any police station regardless of jurisdiction, and CCTV near the spot is only kept for a limited window.

quiz.question: About how much were the fake and expired medicines seized at a Bengaluru repacking unit this week worth?
quiz.why: Bengaluru chemists say such counterfeit stock is unlikely to move through licensed retail pharmacies at all, pointing instead to hospitals and online sellers as the likelier route into circulation.

quiz.question: By when is BMRCL's elevated Pink Line expected to open, per today's news?
quiz.why: Before any new metro line can open to the public, it must clear a mandatory independent safety inspection by the Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety.

quiz.question: At a meeting convened by Amit Shah, Karnataka's CM said how much Mekedatu dam water would be held back for Bengaluru's drinking needs, with the rest going to Tamil Nadu?
quiz.why: TMC (thousand million cubic feet) is the standard unit India uses to measure river-water sharing volumes in inter-state disputes such as the long-running Cauvery/Mekedatu dispute.

quiz.question: What is the sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy called?
quiz.why: India's central bank, the RBI, targets retail inflation (CPI) at around 4%, with a tolerance band of 2–6%, when it sets interest rates.

quiz.question: Which gas do plants primarily take in from the air during photosynthesis?
quiz.why: Photosynthesis also releases oxygen as a byproduct — one reason forests and even city tree cover measurably improve local air quality.
